name_zh: 掌上自主跟拍无人机（现成品基线）
name_en: Palm follow drone baseline (HoverAir X1 PROMAX / Neo 2 class)
one_liner: Buy-today 150-195 g follow drone carried in a chest/shoulder holster; the bar every other aerial concept must beat.
principle: Battery quadrotor, vision-based subject tracking, palm launch/land at stops.

architecture.energy: onboard Li-ion ~12.99 Wh (implied by vendor time)
architecture.sensing: camera vision tracking (+ limited obstacle sensing)
architecture.use_flow: stop -> glove off/partial -> palm launch -> select mode -> ski -> stop -> palm catch -> stow

viewpoints.notes: vendor side mode, obstacle-blind on the far side
rear obstacle sensing only in limited modes 1.5-3 m/s (doc 18)

tilt_limited_airspeed.ref: T/W=2 assumed; shows cap is perception, not thrust

KE_at_20.ref: FAA Cat 2 threshold 11 ft-lbf = 14.9 J for comparison

footage.why: Good external rear/side views at 4-8 m, but vendor follow cap ~12 m/s covers ~60 % of riding time; vision loss in flat light, spray, trees.

interference.why: Nothing on the body during flight; ~0.2 kg in a pocket.

convenience.why: ~9 min per cold battery at 12 m/s; stop to launch/catch; glove gestures unreliable; snow landings need retrieval.

safety.why: Light (14 J @12 m/s) but props near people; unaware of other skiers behind the subject.

bold_hypothesis: A ski-specific holster + workflow alone makes today's palm drones good enough, so new hardware is unjustified.
falsification_test: 10 runs on a permitted slope at 8, 12, 15 m/s with GoPro-on-helmet ground truth: measure % time subject fully in frame and number of lost-track events; kill hypothesis if >20 % runs lose track or <60 % frame-in at 12 m/s.
kill_criteria: Usable continuous footage <60 % of run at 12 m/s
Launch+catch overhead >30 s with gloves
Resort policy forbids use at target venues (already true at Vail Resorts properties)

sim_plan.what_to_model: 6-DoF-lite quad (point mass + attitude first-order lag, thrust/tilt limit, drag), vision tracker with FOV, latency, dropout probability vs contrast/occlusion, follow-speed cap

name_zh: 轨迹复现跟拍机（≤249 g 涵道+可穿戴信标）
name_en: Track-replay follow drone: <=249 g ducted + wearable UWB/GNSS beacon
one_liner: Drone flies the skier's own just-skied path 0.3-2 s later at 3 m above snow, located by a wearable beacon instead of vision, so obstacles at skier height are cleared by construction.
principle: The skier's trajectory is a recently-verified free corridor; replaying it with a time lag dt=d/v plus altitude offset gives a rear-elevated shot without needing general obstacle avoidance. Relative position from UWB ranging + RTK-GNSS/IMU fusion; vision only for framing.

architecture.carrier: 245 g ducted quad (4x76 mm), ducts = prop guards
architecture.sensing: UWB anchor in backpack + IMU/GNSS beacon (~30 g), downward ToF, forward camera
architecture.use_flow: pull from shoulder dock (magnetic) -> throw-up launch -> auto-replay follow -> at stop hovers 3 m away -> 'come home' button on strap -> lands into raised palm or on snow next to skier

viewpoints.notes: lateral offset <=2 m from track only where snow surface is open (beacon map)

replay_lag_5ms_10m.ref: slow skier -> long lag, use shorter d

stop_distance_if_skier_falls_12ms.ref: must stop above, not onto, a fallen skier: replay altitude 3 m keeps 1.5-2 m vertical clearance

footage.why: Follows 5-20 m/s with physics margin; corridor logic keeps it tracking through tree-lined pistes where vision followers drop; view is mostly rear (side views limited).

interference.why: ~30 g beacon + dock on strap; no forces during flight.

convenience.why: ~8 min at 12 m/s cold -> 2-3 runs per battery; needs stop to launch; button recall glove-friendly.

safety.why: Ducted props; 49 J at 20 m/s; corridor replay avoids static obstacles but not other skiers entering the track; resort bans.

simplicity.why: New airframe + beacon fusion + replay planner; failure modes: beacon dropout, GNSS multipath under trees, overhanging branches.

bold_hypothesis: Following the skier's own track (time-shifted) removes >80 % of the obstacle-avoidance problem, which is the real reason vendors cap follow speed at ~12 m/s.
falsification_test: Log skier GNSS/UWB tracks on 20 tree-lined runs; replay virtually at 3 m altitude with 0.3 m noise against a LiDAR/photogrammetry tree map; count corridor violations (branch within 1 m). Then fly real replay on an empty, permitted slope at 12-16 m/s and compare lost-frame % to A01.
kill_criteria: Corridor violations >1 per 10 runs in mapped glades
UWB/GNSS relative error >0.5 m at 95 % in trees
Cannot stay <=249 g with ducts + gimbal + 20 min-class battery
No legal venue for the target user (resort bans + VLOS)

sim_plan.what_to_model: quad dynamics with tilt/thrust limits, beacon measurement noise/dropout, track buffer & lag controller, trees/overhangs as obstacles, second skier crossing the track

name_zh: 背包供电短系留旋翼（飞行摄影杆）
one_liner: Battery-less 180 g quad on a 1.4 mm power tether from an auto-reel on the pack: a virtual selfie boom of 3-10 m with 30-55 min cold endurance.
principle: Move the battery to the body (where mass is cheap) and send power up a 48-100 V micro-tether; the tether also bounds the flight volume and makes recovery a reel-in.

architecture.energy: 60-100 Wh pack battery (0.4-0.65 kg) in backpack
architecture.sensing: tether length/angle encoder gives relative pose; camera for framing
architecture.use_flow: pull strap -> drone lifts from pack lid cradle -> reel pays out to set length -> ski -> stop: reel winds drone back into cradle (docking = reel-in, latch)

viewpoints.notes: tether passes beside skier, visible as thin line
possible at low speed only; tether crosses face/body

stop_distance_vs_tether.ref: drone stop distance from 12 m/s exceeds 3-6 m tether -> reel must free-wheel or 15 N weak link breaks

footage.why: Close 3-10 m rear/side views, 30-55 min; tether visible in frame and range limited -> less environment than A02.

interference.why: ~1 kg on back, 2-3 N tug, <1 N*m yaw; drone motion couples into pack.

convenience.why: No battery swaps on drone; launch/recover by reel without hands; works while moving.

safety.why: Rotors 3-10 m from own head; tether can catch other skiers, lift towers, trees; fall dynamics need weak link.

simplicity.why: Reel tension control + HV tether + docking + flight control.

bold_hypothesis: A 100 V micro-tether costs <5 % power and <2 N at ski speeds, so a battery-less 180 g quad becomes an endless, hands-free selfie boom.
falsification_test: Bench: 6 m tether, 100 V, 75 W, measure loss and heating at -10 C; cart test on a vehicle at 12-20 m/s measuring tether tension and drone attitude; snag test with a weak link on a mannequin fall.
kill_criteria: Tether tension spikes >15 N in normal turns
Reel-in docking success <95 % at 3 m/s relative wind
Any tether-wrap incident on rider in fall tests
Tether visible enough to ruin >30 % of frames

sim_plan.what_to_model: quad + discretised tether (lumped-mass, 10-20 nodes, drag per segment), active reel with tension control, weak link, backpack anchor attached to skier kinematics
scenarios: carved turns with drone outside of turn
tree on inside of turn (tether snag)

name_zh: 背包发射杆风筝（现有概念复核）
name_en: Backpack launch-boom kite (existing sim concept, re-checked)
one_liner: Passive 0.25 m2 kite with 360 camera launched from a pack boom, riding the skier's apparent wind on an 8 m tether.
principle: Skier speed supplies the airflow; L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL supports 0.3 kg above ~6 m/s.

architecture.use_flow: strap pull raises boom -> push off -> kite leaves cradle at release force -> payout -> crank retrieval -> dock latch

viewpoints.notes: tether nearly vertical at L/D~4.4: mostly top-down view

subject_px_360_5.7K.ref: 11.9 deg angular size @16 px/deg; seen largely from above

footage.why: Top-down 74 deg view, ~190 px subject in 360 source; continuity broken below 6 m/s.

interference.why: 12-38 N rear-up pull scaling with V^2, +/-56 % per 3 m/s gust.

convenience.why: No flight battery; but every stop lands/drops the kite; crank retrieval.

safety.why: No rotors; 34 J; tether + kite over the piste near lifts.

simplicity.why: Passive; boom mechanism the main complexity.

bold_hypothesis: Apparent wind from skiing alone is a sufficient, free lift source for a camera.
falsification_test: Tow test (vehicle or skier) at 4-20 m/s logging tension and kite position; measure % of a real run time with airspeed > v_min using GNSS logs from 10 recreational runs.
kill_criteria: Usable airborne time <70 % of run
Peak tension >40 N on pack in gusts
Docking success <90 %
View elevation always >60 deg (no environmental shot)

sim_plan.what_to_model: already in sim/: add attitude dynamics (replace beta blend), depower/bridle control, stall/low-speed regime, ground contact
scenarios: skier stop -> kite descent path vs head

name_zh: 侧飞水翼式风筝（侧位低机位）
one_liner: Steer the kite's lift sideways so it flies ~8 m abeam and 2 m behind at low height, giving the classic side tracking shot without motors.
principle: On a tether the kite sits on a cone of half-angle atan(L/D)~77 deg around the downwind axis; rolling the lift vector horizontal moves it from overhead to abeam, needing only ~14 deg vertical lift share at 12 m/s.

architecture.carrier: 0.3 kg kite with roll servo (or bridle), camera
architecture.sensing: IMU + tether angle for roll control

viewpoints.notes: the cinematic side shot; tether almost horizontal

tether_height.ref: horizontal 8 m line across adjacent track

footage.why: Low side view at ~8 m is the most desired framing (~430 px at 4K).

interference.why: 14-25 N sideways tug that reverses with every turn; ~2 cm CoM-equivalent bias.

convenience.why: Needs roll control and side swaps every turn; lands at every stop.

safety.why: Head-height clothesline across 8 m of piste - unacceptable near other skiers, trees, lift lines.

simplicity.why: Active roll control on a passive kite; turn transitions unsolved.

bold_hypothesis: A tethered kite can hold a side station at skier height using lateral lift alone.
falsification_test: Tow-cart test with roll-servo kite on 8 m line at 8-16 m/s: hold side station +/-1 m for 30 s; then simulate S-turns.
kill_criteria: Any use near other skiers (tether clothesline) - effectively kills product use on open pistes
Station-keeping error >2 m
Kite crosses behind skier at each turn (tether sweeps body)

sim_plan.what_to_model: kite with roll control (lift vector angle), tether lumped-mass, skier S-turns, other-skier agents

name_zh: 混合动力系留翼（风筝-无人机）
name_en: Hybrid kite-drone: tethered tail-sitter wing with thrust assist
one_liner: A 330 g tail-sitter flying wing on a backpack tether: hovers on two props when slow or stopped, becomes a near-zero-power kite above ~8 m/s airspeed.
principle: Wing lift costs ~3 W of control power at ski speeds vs ~65 W for a quad of similar mass; props fill the kite's low-speed dead zone and give attitude control, solving A04's v_min and docking problems.

architecture.carrier: 330 g flying wing S=0.12 m2, 2x130 mm props, elevons
architecture.energy: 60 g onboard pack (optionally power over tether as in A03)
architecture.sensing: IMU, airspeed, tether angle/length; camera framing
architecture.use_flow: hover-launch from pack cradle -> payout -> transitions to kite mode automatically -> at stops hovers at 3-4 m -> reel-in docking with props assisting

viewpoints.notes: props let it sit lower than a passive kite (thrust can pull down/aft)
lateral station by roll, tether away from neighbours

footage.why: Stable rear-high to rear-quarter 6-10 m, continuous through stops; tether in frame.

convenience.why: ~30 min per battery, auto transitions, hands-free dock; complex start-up checks.

safety.why: Props + tether + 37 J; tether over piste.

simplicity.why: Tethered tail-sitter transitions in gusts are a hard control problem; many failure modes.

bold_hypothesis: Combining kite and drone removes each one's fatal flaw: the kite's low-speed dead zone and the drone's 8-10 min endurance.
falsification_test: Simulate then tow-test a 330 g tail-sitter on 8 m tether: measure electrical power vs airspeed 0-20 m/s and transition success in 2 m/s RMS gusts; kill if power >15 W at 12 m/s or transitions fail >2 %.
kill_criteria: Power at 12 m/s airspeed >15 W (no endurance gain)
Transition failure >2 % in gusts
Tether tension cannot be held <20 N at 20 m/s
Mass >400 g after structure+camera

sim_plan.what_to_model: 6-DoF tail-sitter with post-stall aero table (flat-plate model), prop thrust & slipstream, lumped-mass tether, reel, mode logic
scenarios: start from stop and accelerate 0->15 m/s
loss of tracking (fly by tether angle only)

name_zh: 旋翼风筝（自转旋翼系留）
one_liner: Replace the kite wing with a 0.6 m autorotating rotor that folds compactly and descends slowly when wind is lost.
principle: Autorotating rotor produces resultant force ~0.9 x q x disc area with L/D ~3.

architecture.use_flow: spin-up on boom (or pre-spin motor) -> payout -> crank in

v_min.ref: C_R 0.9, L/D 3 assumed from autogyro literature ranges

descent_on_wind_loss.ref: ~same as flat kite (4.4) -> no real safety gain

safety.why: Spinning 0.6 m blades ~30 m/s tip near head on retrieval.

bold_hypothesis: Autorotation makes a safer, more compact apparent-wind carrier than a wing.
falsification_test: Tow test comparing rotor vs delta at equal stowed volume: v_min, tension, descent rate on cut-off, camera vibration PSD.
kill_criteria: Descent rate on wind loss not < 0.6x flat kite (calc says ~1.0x)
Camera vibration >0.5 deg RMS at 16 Hz
Rotor strikes in retrieval

sim_plan.what_to_model: rotor as actuator disc with tilt-dependent C_R and L/D table, spin-up dynamics, tether

name_zh: 机会镜头微型飞行器（只拍高光段）
one_liner: 90 g flyer stored in a shoulder pod; launched only at the top of a chosen pitch for one scripted 20-40 s shot, then lands next to the stopped skier.
principle: Spend flight energy and regulatory exposure only on the 10 % of the run worth filming; a body camera covers the rest.

architecture.use_flow: stop at top -> one-button pod release -> drone hovers 4 m in front (establishing) -> skier drops in -> 20-40 s follow -> skier stops -> drone lands within 3 m / hand catch -> back to pod (charges from pack)

shots_per_battery_cold.ref: pod recharge from pack raises this

footage.why: Excellent highlight shots but not continuous.

convenience.why: ~20-25 s overhead per shot; few shots per charge unless pod charges.

simplicity.why: Small airframe, scripted shot reduces autonomy demands.

bold_hypothesis: Users value 3-6 great 30 s shots per day more than continuous mediocre follow footage.
falsification_test: User study: give 8 skiers either continuous A01 follow or highlight-only mode for a day; measure clips kept/shared and perceived hassle.
kill_criteria: Per-shot overhead >40 s
Landing within 5 m of skier <90 %
Users keep fewer clips than with continuous mode

sim_plan.what_to_model: A01/A02 dynamics + scripted shot library + landing near stopped skier on slope

one_liner: Clip a 0.5 mm, 4 g, 20 m Dyneema leash on a spring reel between pack and a palm drone: bounded fly-away, pull-back recovery from snow, minimal drag.
principle: The leash gives the safety/recovery value of a tether at <1 N drag, keeping the drone's own battery.

architecture.sensing: leash length encoder as backup relative range
architecture.use_flow: clip -> launch -> reel free-runs with light tension -> after landing in powder: reel in

drag_20m_20ms_side.ref: = 1.3x weight of 192 g drone: significant at high speed

convenience.why: Easier recovery; but leash management, tangles.

safety.why: No fly-away; leash can snag others; still a UA legally.

falsification_test: Drag/tangle test at 12-20 m/s with 10-20 m leash; count tangles per hour and flight-time penalty.
kill_criteria: Tangles >1 per hour
Flight time penalty >20 % at 16 m/s

name_zh: 轻于空气（氦气球）载具/升力辅助
one_liner: Helium balloon carrying the camera on a tether, or a small balloon to unload a quad.
principle: Buoyancy ~0.91 kg/m3 net at 2000 m, -10 C.
bold_hypothesis: Buoyancy can remove the energy cost of holding a camera aloft.
falsification_test: Already falsified by calc: drag at ski speed exceeds buoyant lift by 50-100x.

name_zh: 固定翼跟拍机（远景巡航）
one_liner: 300 g flying wing follows the skier's smoothed path at 15-25 m, loitering in 8-13 m circles when the skier stops; ~1 h endurance.
principle: At ski speeds, a wing at L/D 7 needs ~10 W vs ~65 W for a quad.

architecture.carrier: 300 g foam flying wing S=0.12 m2, pusher prop
architecture.use_flow: hand-launch -> autonomous follow/orbit -> belly-land in soft snow near skier

viewpoints.notes: can't hold a station; flies figure-8s/arcs

footage.why: Wide, environment-rich but small subject and periodic framing.

convenience.why: Hand launch on slope, belly landing in snow, no hover at stops.

simplicity.why: Follow planner for non-hovering aircraft + landing.

bold_hypothesis: Endurance, not framing, is the limiting factor for aerial ski filming, so a wing beats rotors.
falsification_test: Sim: compare % usable frames of fixed-wing vs A02 over 20 recorded ski tracks.
kill_criteria: Usable framed time <50 %
Landing damage >10 % of flights

sim_plan.what_to_model: fixed-wing 3-DoF with bank/speed limits, path-following to a predicted skier reference

name_zh: 翼面卸载背负摄影杆（体载升力面）
one_liner: A 0.12 m2 wing at the tip of a 1.6 m pack mast carries the camera's weight in the apparent wind.
principle: Small lift surface cancels tip weight moment at speed (O09 revisited with numbers).

gust_root_moment_swing.ref: what the wing adds per 3 m/s gust

interference.why: Gust moment swing > static moment saved.

bold_hypothesis: Aerodynamic unloading makes a long mast feel weightless.
falsification_test: Calc already shows gust-induced moment swing (6.2 N*m) exceeds the static moment removed (3.9 N*m).
kill_criteria: Killed by calc unless an active/feathering wing is used
